annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on 'Proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)'
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on the Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 140
annotation.summary_en: EESC opinion supporting the Commission's AI Liability Directive proposal, which introduces a rebuttable presumption of causality and access to evidence for victims of AI harm. It urges clearer definitions, alternative dispute resolution, monitoring of insurance, and an earlier three-year review. It briefly addresses autonomous vehicle insurance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Supports presumption of causality and right of access to evidence for victims of AI damage
Calls for clear definitions of high-risk AI and eligible damage, and judicial training
Advocates free, mandatory alternative dispute resolution with EU-wide coordination
Recommends monitoring insurance and incident reporting before considering strict liability or mandatory insurance
Recommends review after 3 years rather than 5; no further action needed where compulsory insurance exists, e.g. autonomous vehicles
